title: Staged operator migration with health-gated control plane upgrades
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: We need an automated, auditable path to upgrade the Private control plane operator and runtime components across customer VPCs with minimal blast radius. This ticket implements a staged operator migration that combines Terraform module-driven orchestration, GitOps-style version registry, and health-gated traffic sampling to promote candidate versions.

Background: Several recent incident post-mortems identified edge cases where a full-cluster operator upgrade caused KV cache incompatibilities and transient API failures. Current manual upgrade steps are slow and error-prone for large fleets. Previous tickets introduced canary probes and phased rollouts, but we lack an integrated Terraform/IaC workflow and clear health gates.

Goals:
- Provide an automated upgrade pipeline that is reproducible via Terraform modules and state manipulations.
- Reduce mean time to safely promote a control plane version from validation -> staged -> global.
- Ensure strong, measurable health gates (SLO-based) with automatic rollback when thresholds are breached.
- Keep upgrades auditable and reversible; ensure minimal customer impact.

Proposed approach:
1) Version Registry: maintain a Git-backed JSON manifest (versions.yaml) in the control-plane-ops repo that declares candidate images, feature flags, and compatibility notes. Terraform modules will reference a pinned manifest entry by tag.
2) Terraform orchestration: extend existing private deployment modules with a new submodule operator_upgrade that:
   - accepts inputs: target_version, traffic_weight (0-100), max_unhealthy_pods, health_checks (list of check ids).
   - creates a staged Deployment/DaemonSet update plan via a temporary staging namespace per cluster.
   - writes progress to a central terraform state plus a per-customer upgrade record in the infra-state S3 bucket.
3) GitOps promotion: after Terraform applies the staging change, a validation job (K8s job in staging namespace) runs integration smoke tests and calls the promotion webhook if all checks pass.
4) Traffic gating and rollout: use a traffic-splitting sidecar/route object inside the control plane API mesh to divert a configurable percentage of control-plane requests to the new operator instance. Traffic ramps are driven by the terraform plan (traffic_weight increments).

Health gates and checks:
- Define a health-check catalog (health-check IDs) with a canonical implementation that includes: API latency percentile (p95 < 120ms), error rate (<0.5% 5m), reconciliation success rate (>99% per minute), KV cache miss ratio delta (<2% relative to baseline), control-plane self-heal time (<30s).
- Run health checks continuously for staged clusters with a 5m evaluation window.
- Promotion conditions: three consecutive 5m windows meeting all gates at current traffic weight AND no critical alerts.
- Rollback conditions: any single 5m window showing critical violation (customer-facing error spike, reconciliation failure) triggers immediate rollback to previous version and notifies on-call.

Terraform/IaC implementation notes:
- Keep module interfaces stable; add operator_upgrade as an opt-in change to avoid disrupting existing flows.
- Use remote-exec triggers sparingly; prefer declarative resources and Kubernetes jobs.
- Store upgrade metadata in a new table in infra-state (s3-backed JSON) so other subsystems (console, audit) can query upgrade history.
- Provide a migration helper script for existing state where operator control plane was managed outside modules.

Observability and dashboards:
- Add an Upgrade Health dashboard per-customer with: current target_version, traffic_weight, health metrics, last_promotion_event, rollback_count.
- Create a composite alert when any promotion fails or when a rollback occurs. Alerts index the upgrade record id for quick triage.

Security and compliance:
- All version manifests must be signed by release engineering keys.
- Terraform plans for upgrades require approval in the infra repo (protected branches) and an RFC link in the PR description.
- Ensure KMS-wrapped secrets are not exposed in upgrade logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A terraform module PR implementing operator_upgrade is merged and documented.
- A non-production cluster has completed a staged upgrade from vA -> vB with traffic ramping from 0->20->50->100 without health gate violations.
- An automated rollback is executed in a simulated failure test and recorded in infra-state.
- Console shows upgrade history for that customer and links to logs/PR.

Open questions / Risks:
- Sidecar-based traffic splitting adds complexity to the control plane networking; need a safety fallback if mesh update fails.
- How do we handle stateful operator data migrations (schema changes that require in-place migration)? Consider migration hooks that run once before traffic ramp.
- Terraform concurrency: multiple parallel upgrades for the same cluster need locking to avoid state races.

Next steps / Tasks:
- Design doc in Confluence: control-plane-upgrade-strategy (owner: Sofia). Link: https://confluence.company/repo/control-plane-upgrade-strategy (WIP).
- Implement terraform submodule skeleton and unit tests. (owner: Liam)
- Build health-check harness and baseline scripts for measurement. (owner: Reliability team)
- Draft runbook for on-call rollback and manual promotion steps.

Notes: keep upgrade steps as declarative as possible and favor observability at each step. This implementation should serve as the canonical upgrade path for Private control plane versions and be extensible to Dedicated deployments later.
